chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The cavalry horses used to be wild in the Arab lands, so Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) ascended Mount Jiyad, then they shouted: 'Do not be loose, do not be loose!' He said: 'So there did not remain a horse excepted no horse but that it gave its hand (foreleg) to them and enabled its forelock (to be touched by them).'

key_terms.أَلَا هَلَا: An exclamation meaning 'Do not be loose/free' or 'Stand firm'
key_terms.جَبَلِ جِيَادٍ: Mount Jiyad (a specific mountain associated with horses)
key_terms.نَاصِيَتِهِ: Its forelock (the hair on the forehead of a horse)

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Ibrahim and Ismail tame the wild horses of Arabia?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual authority of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail (AS) over nature, specifically the taming of wild horses in pre-Islamic Arabia, serving as a foundational precedent for the merit of bridling cavalry. The chain of transmission through Aban and Zurara to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores its reliability within the Shia scholarly tradition, linking this historical event to the practical virtues of horsemanship and archery discussed in the chapter.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The cavalry horses used to be wild in the Arab countries, so Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> and Ismail<sup>as</sup> ascended upon mount Jiyad, then they both<sup>as</sup> shouted: ‘Do not be loose, do not be loose!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So there did not remain a horse except that it gave its hand (front leg) to both of them<sup>as</sup>, and enabled its forelock (to be touched by them both<sup>as</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from more than one narrator from Aban from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

horses were wild in Arab lands. Once, Ibrahim and Isma’il ‘Alayhima al-Salam, climbed on Jiyad hills. They then called, £ 0 horses come home.’ He (the Imam) then said, ’Every horse then allowed the two of them to touch their legs and forehead.’”
